title: My Life in Mongolia and Siberia
subtitle: From the Great Wall of China to the Ural Mountains
short_title: My Life in Mongolia and Siberia
summary: John Sheepshanks, later Bishop of Norwich, had spent more than six years as a clergyman on the Fraser River in British Columbia when he set out for England by the Pacific, China and the continent of Asia, wanting to see the missions of the Russian Church in Siberia. Written up in 1903 from the journal he kept, the book follows him from the frontier town of Chang-kia-keu in August across the Mongolian steppe and desert by cart and camel with two Mongol guides, to the sacred city of Ourga (Urga) and its temples and its incarnate god, the Khutuktu, then north by Kiachta, the Selenga and Lake Baikal to Irkutsk, and by the post-road across Siberia to the Urals. One chapter describes Shamanism. The year of the journey (1867) is not printed; it is taken from accounts of his life.
